drhp.business: Reliance Power develops, constructs and operates power generation projects in India, supported by integrated captive coal resources and long-term power offtake arrangements. Its portfolio is predominantly large-scale coal-based thermal generation, complemented by solar PV, concentrated solar and wind assets. Its customers are power distribution companies, which in turn supply power to end consumers.

litigation.note: The Directors' Report section 'Material Changes and Commitments' discloses actions initiated against the Company and subsidiaries by various regulatory authorities: search and seizure by the Directorate of Enforcement under PMLA; the arrest of Shri Ashok Kumar Pal, former Executive Director and CFO, and a supplementary prosecution complaint filed against the Company, two subsidiaries and two employees in the matter of an alleged false bank guarantee submitted to SECI; an FIR registered by the Economic Offences Wing of Delhi Police on a SECI complaint; provisional attachment of certain assets by ED, confirmed after year-end by the Adjudicating Authority under PMLA for 365 days; a SEBI Show Cause Notice dated September 30, 2025 alleging violations of the SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations; a further SEBI Show Cause Notice dated April 10, 2026 alleging violations of Regulation 30 and Regulations 4(1)(c) and 4(1)(e) of the Listing Regulations; and a SEBI-initiated forensic audit of the Company by letter dated January 14, 2026. The Company states it and its employees acted bona-fidely and are victims of fraud, forgery, cheating and conspiracy by third parties, and continues to cooperate with the authorities. The Directors also draw attention to the impact of Audit Qualifications on the Consolidated Financial Statements.

risks.note: The auditors draw attention to Note 28 of the standalone financial statements: the lender of Samalkot Power Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, has invoked the corporate guarantee against the Company and demanded payment of overdue dues, and has initiated the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process against the Company under section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The auditors state these events and conditions indicate a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on the Company's ability to continue as a going concern, although the accounts have been prepared on a going-concern basis and the opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.
risks.risk: Material uncertainty related to going concern — corporate guarantee invoked and insolvency proceedings initiated against the Company

risks.note: The auditors' Emphasis of Matters draws attention to Note 33(a) describing ongoing proceedings initiated by the Directorate of Enforcement under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. The Directors' Report records search and seizure by ED, the arrest of the former Executive Director and CFO in the matter of an alleged false bank guarantee submitted to SECI, a supplementary prosecution complaint against the Company, two subsidiaries and two employees, an FIR by the Economic Offences Wing of Delhi Police on a SECI complaint, and provisional attachment of certain assets of the Company and its subsidiaries, confirmed after year-end by the Adjudicating Authority for 365 days. The Company states it and its employees acted bona-fidely and are victims of fraud, forgery, cheating and conspiracy by third parties.
risks.risk: Enforcement Directorate proceedings under PMLA, including asset attachment and prosecution of the Company, subsidiaries and employees

risks.note: A Show Cause Notice dated September 30, 2025 alleges violations of the SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, 2003 read with the SEBI Act, 1992; a further Show Cause Notice dated April 10, 2026 alleges violations of Regulation 30 and Regulations 4(1)(c) and 4(1)(e) of the Listing Regulations; and SEBI, by letter dated January 14, 2026, initiated a forensic audit of the Company in connection with alleged violations of the SEBI Act, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act and the Companies Act.
risks.risk: SEBI enforcement exposure — two Show Cause Notices and a SEBI-initiated forensic audit

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table identifies Regulatory Issues as both an opportunity and a risk: the power sector and the Company's projects are heavily regulated in terms of operations and tariff recoveries, and the Company is engaged with State and Central regulators for adjudication of various disputes with power procurers, which could have positive or negative implications for operations. Mitigation is limited to advocacy through industry associations.
risks.risk: Regulatory and tariff-recovery risk in a heavily regulated power sector

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table flags that thermal power generation entails emissions of SOx, NOx and CO2 and the need to dispose of large quantities of ash, and that failure to comply with the norms could lead to negative impact and penalties. The Company states it operates well within approved emission parameters.
risks.risk: Environmental emissions and ash disposal from thermal generation, with penalty exposure on non-compliance

risks.note: The BRSR table records that the nature of the business is subject to high risk of safety hazards, mitigated through regular safety training for employees and third-party contract workers plus periodic safety audits and inspections; and separately that any incident at a project or industrial action by workers can lead to operational disruptions. The scale is material — the Company reports 6,321 other-than-permanent workers against 1,278 permanent employees.
risks.risk: Workforce safety and labour relations at project sites

risks.note: The BRSR table identifies the risk of security breaches gaining access to information systems due to internet exposure, mitigated by an Integrated Intrusion Detection and Prevention Monitoring System with auto monitoring, log monitoring, security patch monitoring and alerting, encryption of incoming and outgoing communication, and employee awareness campaigns.
risks.risk: Cyber security risk to information systems

risks.note: The Directors' Report records an unusually heavy churn in FY26: the Executive Director and CFO resigned on October 11, 2025 due to his arrest and pending investigation, with the CEO given additional charge as interim CFO; two directors resigned with effect from August 29, 2025 and another on November 03, 2025; several additional directors were appointed during and after the year; and thirteen Board meetings were held during the financial year. The Company also concentrates the CEO and CFO roles in one person, and the statutory auditors are changing at the ensuing AGM.
risks.risk: Board and senior-management instability, including the loss of the CFO to arrest
